Case B (from research): Empty → first artifact → habit. Prefer air + one CTA + template → return to density. Reject permanent empty illustration and hard commit with no revert. Measure time-to-first-artifact and D7 return.

10.8 Optimistic vs pessimistic decision matrix

Context Bias Why
Star, pin, draft create Optimistic + soft undo Cheap rollback
Archive personal item Optimistic + soft undo or quarantine Reversible
Delete shared / team-visible Quarantine or hard confirm Blast radius
Checkout / charge Pessimistic + idempotent Trust × frequency (L14)
Mass notify / email Pessimistic or Undo Send window External irreversibility
AI mutate file / send Diff → apply → undo (Ch. 14) Silent mutation destroys trust

Case A — Checkout: pessimistic; field errors; receipt. Reject optimistic “Paid!” before bank. Measure payment success, error recovery, keyboard completion, chargebacks.

Case C — Shared destructive delete: confirm with blast radius or Trash 30d if recoverable. Reject soft toast for team-visible destroy. Focus trap + announced result + restore focus to trigger.

10.9 Chapter 10 summary

  • Acknowledge ≤100ms; tier the wait; never blank the page for a click.
  • Classify every mutation: soft / quarantine / hard.
  • Design the seven states; then specialize empty vs zero vs error vs denied with distinct copy and CTAs.
  • Optimistic when rollback is cheap; pessimistic on money, legal, and shared blast.

Forms & auth playbook (expanded)

Concern Rule
Labels Visible always; never placeholder-as-label
Validation Blur for format; submit for required set; preserve input on error
Errors Field-local + optional GOV.UK Error Summary (linked list)
Layout Trust paths = 1-column; paired short fields may 2-col on wide CQ
Double-submit Disable + in-place pending; idempotent keys on pay/create-once
Auth autocomplete correct; passkeys/OTP > passwords alone; PM-friendly
CAPTCHA Accessible alternative always (Case F); no puzzle-only
Session Warn before timeout; extend; restore drafts where safe

Typeahead / combobox: Prefer native <datalist> or full APG combobox (arrow keys, typeahead, aria-activedescendant). Don’t fake autocomplete with divs.

Offline matrix:

Mode UI
Read-only offline Banner; disable mutating controls with explanation
Queue offline Banner “changes queued”; syncing state on flush
Conflict Keep both / choose / merge prefer-when (Ch 14)

Chapter 11 — Search, Filter, Sort & Pagination

Finding work is half of product interaction. Cmd-K is a power palette—not a substitute for a search product. This chapter covers the information-seeking kit flagged as a critical gap: query, scope, empty/zero results, ranking honesty, faceted refine, URL persistence, and pagination vs infinite scroll vs load-more.

11.1 Findability system map

Surface Job Typical entry
Global search / Cmd-K Jump to object or action Keyboard; spotlight
In-place search Narrow current list Search field above list/table
Filters / facets Constrain by attributes Chips, sidebar, sheet
Sort Order by relevance or field Column header / select
Pagination / scroll Traverse the result set Pager, load more, infinite

Treat these as one system: changing search, filter, or sort should update the same result region, the same URL (when shareable), and the same zero-state recovery.

11.2 Search product requirements

Cmd-K ≠ search product. A complete search experience needs:

  1. Query — what the user typed; visible; clearable.
  2. Scope — where we look (this project, all projects, people, files, actions). Default scope must be obvious.
  3. Results — ranked list with type labels; keyboard navigation; open on Enter.
  4. Empty query state — recent, suggested, or actions—not a blank void.
  5. Zero results — honest “No matches for query”; offer clear search, change scope, or spelling help—not popular items disguised as matches.
  6. Ranking honesty — do not silently rewrite the query; if you fall back (e.g. stem, fuzzy), say so.
  7. Error / denied — distinct from zero (Ch. 10 taxonomy).
  8. Performance — acknowledge keystroke; debounce network; show pending without layout thrash.

Steal: Linear Cmd-K for action+object jump; keep a progressive path for users who never learn the shortcut (visible Search in chrome).

11.3 Filter & faceted refine

Pattern Prefer when Notes
Chip filters Few active dimensions; always visible Removable chips; “Clear all”
Filter sheet (mobile) Many facets; small viewport Apply/Cancel; show count preview
Sidebar facets Desktop power tools; high density Sticky; URL-synced
Inline column filters Tables with known columns Don’t hide behind mystery icons only

Rules:

  • Active filters must be visible—never invisible constraints.
  • Filtered-to-zero uses Clear filters CTA (Ch. 10.7).
  • Show result count when filters change (“12 of 480”).
  • Persist filters in the URL for shareable/deep-linkable views unless privacy forbids (then session storage + explicit “Save view”).
  • Facet counts should not lie: if a facet would yield zero given current selection, disable or show 0—don’t offer dead ends without signal.

11.4 Sort

  • Default sort must match user expectation (often recent activity or relevance under search).
  • Column-header sort: indicate direction; support keyboard; announce change politely.
  • Multi-sort only when power users need it—and show the sort order explicitly.
  • Sorting under an active search: clarify whether sort is relevance-first or field-first; don’t silently drop relevance without a control.

11.5 Pagination vs infinite scroll vs load-more

Pattern Prefer when Avoid when
Paged Need item N; SEO; stable address; tables with row actions Casual browse feeds where page breaks feel arbitrary
Load more User-controlled growth; mobile-friendly When users must reach a known position often
Infinite scroll Discovery feeds; low per-item commitment Footer access; task lists; keyboard/AT heavy tables; restoring exact scroll position across sessions

Hard rules:

  • Infinite scroll must not trap keyboard or screen reader users—provide a load-more peer or virtualization with reachable landmarks.
  • Preserve scroll position and selection across back-navigation when possible.
  • Show total count or “approx.” honesty when known; don’t invent precision.
  • For tables, prefer pagination or virtualized window with sticky header—not infinite append that breaks sticky math and “select all.”

11.6 URL persistence & deep links

Shareable views are part of collaboration (Ch. 13). Encode:

  • q query
  • filters (stable keys, not display labels)
  • sort + direction
  • page or cursor

Prefer cursor-based pagination for large mutable sets; page numbers drift when items insert above. When using cursors, the URL still records the cursor token or opaque after param.

Browser Back: returning from a detail page should restore list query/filter/sort/scroll (history state or URL)—not reset to defaults.

11.7 Search + filter zero-state playbook

State Copy skeleton CTA
Empty query, no filters Recent / Suggested / “Search projects” Focus search; optional browse
Query, 0 hits No matches for “X” Clear search; try scope
Filters, 0 hits No items match these filters Clear filters (list chips)
Query + filters, 0 hits Name both constraints Clear search or filters
Error Couldn’t load results Retry
Denied You don’t have access to search here Request access

11.8 Accessibility & performance notes

  • Search field: visible label (not placeholder-only); role="search" landmark where appropriate.
  • Announce result count changes via polite live region (throttle).
  • Debounce network (~150–300ms); cancel in-flight on new keystroke.
  • Keyboard: arrows through results; Enter opens; Esc clears or closes overlay; focus restore on close (L9).

11.9 Chapter 11 summary

  • Build a findability system: search, filter, sort, pagination share one result region and recovery taxonomy.
  • Cmd-K is a palette; search still needs scope, zero honesty, and ranking honesty.
  • Persist refine state in the URL; make filtered-to-zero recoverable.
  • Choose pager vs load-more vs infinite by task—not fashion; always leave an AT-reachable path.

Chapter 12 — Selection, Tables & Drag-and-Drop

Object manipulation is the other half of work: select, inspect, bulk-act, reorder, edit in place. Selection models, data tables/grids, and drag-and-drop were critical or important gaps in the research audit—this chapter supplies the kit.

12.1 Selection models

Model Behavior Prefer when
Single One selected; click replaces Detail inspector; radio-like choice
Multi-toggle Click toggles; Cmd/Ctrl-click add Sparse multi-select
Shift-range Shift-click selects contiguous range from anchor Lists and tables
Scoped select-all Select all in current filter/page/scope—not the entire universe without warning Bulk toolbars
Marquee Drag rectangle (canvas) Design tools; always provide keyboard alt

Rules:

  • Show N selected in a selection-anchored toolbar (Figma-style contextual chrome).
  • Select-all scope must be explicit: “Select all 25 on this page” vs “Select all 1,842 matching filters.” Confirm or progressive disclose the large scope.
  • Clearing filters does not silently clear selection without notice—or does, but announce it.
  • Selection is keyboardable: Space toggles; Shift+Arrow extends; Ctrl/Cmd+A scoped.
  • Empty selection: hide bulk actions; don’t leave destructive buttons enabled at 0.

12.2 Selection-anchored toolbars

When N > 0:

  • Elevate a contextual bar: primary bulk actions + overflow.
  • Keep the bar near the selection or sticky in a predictable place—don’t cover the first selected row’s checkbox.
  • Partial failure on bulk: keep successes; list failures with retry (Ch. 10).
  • Esc clears selection when focus is in the list region (document the shortcut).

12.3 Data tables & grids

Tables are daily-driver density surfaces (prefer density vs air for power users). They need systems, interaction, and a11y contracts—not just <div> rows.

Structure & semantics

  • Use real <table> (or APG grid when cell navigation is required).
  • Column headers with <th> and scope; associate row headers when first column identifies the row.
  • Sticky header on scroll; ensure contrast and focus not clipped.
  • Don’t rely on color alone for status (L11)—text, icon, or pattern too.

Column behaviors

Behavior Spec notes
Resize Drag handle + keyboard resize; persist widths per user
Reorder Drag column or “Move left/right”; announce new order
Show/hide Column picker; don’t remove required identity columns
Pin / freeze Pin identity column on horizontal scroll
Inline edit Enter edits; Esc cancels; Save/blur commits with undo class
Row actions Visible primary; overflow menu; not hover-only on mobile

Keyboard cell navigation (APG grid when needed)

  • Arrow keys move between cells; Home/End; Page Up/Down when virtualized.
  • Enter activates widget inside cell; F2 or Enter for edit mode if spreadsheet-like.
  • Focus visible ≥2px contrast ring; never outline: none.
  • Sortable headers are buttons in the header cell—announced with sort direction.

Loading & empty in tables

  • Skeleton rows matching column layout.
  • Filtered-to-zero inside the table region with chips above—not a marketing empty state.
  • Error row/region with retry; preserve column setup.

Density

Offer comfortable / compact (and dense if daily pro tool) as token maps, not one-off padding. Density toggle is a Superhuman/Gmail-class mechanic—pair with templates for newcomers so density isn’t elitist.

12.4 Drag-and-Drop (DnD)

DnD is high-delight and high-exclusion risk. Ship the pointer path and a peer path.

Concern Requirement
Visible equivalent Buttons/menus: Move up/down, Move to…
Gesture limit ≤1 swipe action per list row; vertical scroll wins
Desktop reorder Prefer explicit handles—don’t make the whole row ambiguous vs click
Drop targets Clear valid/invalid affordance; multi-channel (not color alone)
Keyboard Pick up / move / drop via APG pattern or move dialog
Screen readers Announce grab, position, drop; live region updates
Touch Long-press carefully; don’t break scroll; ≥44×44 handles
Undo Reorder should be soft-undoable when cheap
Reduced motion Instant reposition without fling theater

Prefer-when:

  • Handles for reorderable lists on desktop.
  • Move-to dialog for accessibility and for deep hierarchies where dragging is error-prone.
  • Confirm when drop crosses permission or irreversible boundary.

Reject: hover-only mobile DnD; drag-only merge for sync conflicts (Case H); color-only drop validity.

12.5 Bulk operations checklist

  1. Scope select-all correctly.
  2. Show N selected + blast preview for destructive bulk.
  3. Idempotent server ops where possible.
  4. Partial success UI.
  5. Undo class matches blast (soft vs quarantine vs hard).
  6. Announce completion via polite status; focus remains sensible.

12.6 Chapter 12 summary

  • Selection is a first-class model: shift-range, scoped select-all, selection-anchored toolbar.
  • Tables need semantics, sticky headers, column ops, inline edit, and keyboard maps—not div soup.
  • DnD always ships with a visible keyboard-accessible equivalent; scroll wins; handles beat mystery grabs.

Chapter 13 — Navigation, History, Disclosure, Teaching, Share, Autosave, Clipboard, Notifications & Collab

This chapter covers the “product conversation” around getting to work and staying oriented: where you are, how you got here, what is hidden, how you learn, how you share, how drafts survive, how paste behaves, how alerts interrupt, and how others appear in the same artifact.

13.1 Navigation shells

Platform Chrome bias Must match across platforms?
Web app Side or top nav; Cmd-K Semantics & IA — yes; chrome — no
iOS Tab bar Native chrome — no pixel parity
Android Nav bar / tabs Native chrome

Dual device models—not shrunk desktop (interaction strategy). Shared semantics and tokens; native gestures and materials.

Scent of core action: primary nav labeled until learnability is proven; icon-only primary nav is an anti-pattern. Quiet chrome / loud content on tool surfaces.

Landmarks: skip link to #main; banner, navigation, main, complementary, contentinfo as appropriate; heading outline h1–h6 reflects IA (a11y structure gap).

13.2 History, deep links & Back

  • Every meaningful object view should be addressable (deep link).
  • Browser Back restores prior list refine state (Ch. 11) and focus where feasible.
  • In-app “back” must not fight the browser history stack—prefer real history transitions.
  • Confirm before discarding dirty state if autosave is off; if autosave is on, Back is safe (see 13.6).
  • After modal close, restore focus to the trigger (L9)—history and focus are cousins.

13.3 Progressive disclosure (L8)

Layer Contents Prefer when
Primary Core path actions Must be found without tour
Overflow Secondary actions Frequent enough to need one click
Palette (Cmd-K / /) Long-tail expert actions Power users; dense tools
Settings Rare preferences Not a dumping ground for features

Failure modes: expert dump on the primary surface or buried core action. Disclosure vs discoverability tension: prefer disclosure for long-tail; prefer discoverability for the critical path.

Context menus and hover cards: never the only path to a core action; hover cards need keyboard peer (focus + delay dismiss that is cancellable).

13.4 Teaching & onboarding curriculum

Reject permanent carousels. Prefer a first-artifact curriculum:

  1. Identity — who you are in the product
  2. Artifact — create one real thing (undoable)
  3. Share — invite or publish once
  4. Return cue — reason to come back (notification, bookmark, unfinished draft)

Empty teaching UI (Ch. 10.7) is part of teaching—templates simulate the future (product playbook). Measure time-to-first-value and find-rate of core action without docs.

Help mechanisms: in-context links, short plain language, and searchable help—not a modal wall on first launch. Cognitive: one primary; predictable chrome.

13.5 Share sheets & ACL

Element Spec
Share entry Obvious on artifact; not buried only in “…”
ACL clarity View / comment / edit named in plain language
Link sharing Distinguish invite vs anyone-with-link; warn on wide ACL
Revoke As clear as grant; audit when enterprise
Confirm Hard confirm when widening from private → public

Share is often external irreversibility (notification to others)—bias pessimistic on send, optimistic on copy link with clear ACL badge.

13.6 Autosave & drafts

Pattern Prefer when
Autosave + version history Documents, canvases, long forms
Explicit Save Legal attestations; rare commits; code deploys
Draft + Publish Content that notifies others on publish

UI requirements:

  • Visible save state: Saved / Saving / Offline queued / Error—map to L6 syncing/offline/error.
  • Never lose input on transient error; retry; preserve local draft.
  • Dirty navigation guard only when data would be lost.
  • Conflict with collab: prefer-when keep both / choose / merge (see 13.10 and Ch. 14 offline).

13.7 Clipboard & paste

  • Copy link / copy value: confirm with soft toast (copied).
  • Paste into rich surfaces: sanitize; don’t execute; show paste preview when risky.
  • Paste permissions (web): request on gesture; explain denial (Ch. 14 permissions pattern).
  • Tables: paste grid into cells with clear mapping; undo one paste as a unit.
  • Password fields: allow paste (password-manager-friendly); don’t block clipboard for false security theater.

13.8 Notifications IA

Tier Behavior Prefer when
Critical interrupt Modal or assertive alert Security, payment failure, data loss
Batched digest Center + optional email digest Social, comments, non-urgent
Muteable Per-type mute; quiet hours for non-critical Anything not safety/billing

Notification center: unread clarity; mark-as-read; deep link to object; empty vs zero (no unread vs never used) distinct.

Rules:

  • Toasts queue; don’t stack focus theft.
  • Email/push preference center is part of trust—not a dark pattern maze.
  • In-app badge counts must match reality; don’t invent urgency (growth vs trust tension).

13.9 Wizards & multi-step flows

  • One primary job per step; progress indicator honest (step N of M).
  • Allow Back without wiping; autosave drafts between steps when long.
  • Error Summary on review step; don’t strand users on step 3 with silent invalid step 1.
  • Prefer progressive disclosure over five-page wizards when fields are few.

13.10 Live collaboration

Signal Role
Presence Who is here (Figma-style conversation)
Cursors / following Optional; never required for edit
Comments / threads Anchored to objects; resolve state
Awareness of edits Field-level or region locks when needed
Conflict UI Keep both / choose / merge — keyboard accessible

Prefer-when for conflicts (Case H):

  • Keep both — equal peer edits, unknown merge
  • Choose — one version clearly stale/wrong
  • Merge — structured fields, no overlapping prose

Reject silent overwrite. Announce remote changes politely; don’t steal focus while typing unless destructive collision needs assertive handling.

13.11 Chapter 13 summary

  • Native nav chrome; shared IA; labeled core scent; real deep links and Back.
  • Disclose long-tail; never bury the critical path; teach via first artifact.
  • Autosave makes state talkative; clipboard and share respect ACL honesty.
  • Notifications are tiered and muteable; collab is presence + conflict prefer-when—not ghost edits.

Chapter 14 — Mobile, Gestures, Permissions, Offline & AI UI

Mobile and AI are where interaction strategy meets platform and trust. Dual device models, JIT permissions, offline sync indicators, and AI propose → review → undo are required—not optional polish.

14.1 Dual device models

Concern Shared across devices Native / distinct
Semantic roles, IA, undo classes Yes —
Gestures, nav chrome, materials — Yes
Density defaults Often distinct Comfortable bias on small screens
Hit targets ≥44×44 primary touch —

Reject: pixel-identical RN fantasy; shrunk-web with hover-only actions. Prefer: sheets + buttons on mobile; hover cards demoted.

Safe areas, notches, and foldables: content and sticky actions respect insets; don’t trap CTAs under home indicators.

14.2 Gestures

Rule Detail
≤1 swipe action per list row Competing edges fight scroll
Visible equivalent always Button/menu peer for every gesture
Vertical scroll wins Don’t hijack the main axis casually
Desktop reorder Handles (Ch. 12)
System gestures Respect iOS swipe-back / Android back; don’t override without strong reason
Discoverability Hint once; don’t rely on hidden gestures for core path
Motor a11y No hold-only exclusive path; pointer cancel; adequate spacing

14.3 Permissions (JIT)

Request permission at the moment of intent—not on first app launch in a bundle of scary dialogs.

Step UI
1. User invokes feature needing capability Camera, location, notifications, clipboard, mic
2. Pre-prompt (optional but recommended) Explain value in product UI before OS dialog
3. OS prompt System sheet
4a. Granted Continue task
4b. Denied Explain + link to settings + feature-degraded path—not a dead end

Denied is an L6 state with a CTA (Ch. 10.7). Never loop the OS prompt endlessly; teach how to re-enable.

14.4 Offline & sync

State Show
Offline Banner: “Offline—changes queued” (or read-only honesty)
Syncing Explicit syncing indicator
Synced Quiet; optional last-synced meta
Conflict Both versions + choose/merge/keep both

Case H: reject silent overwrite; keyboard-accessible conflict UI; syncing belongs in the state matrix—not a mystery spinner.

Prefer-when conflicts: keep both (equal peers) · choose (one stale) · merge (structured fields).

Queue mutations optimistically when safe; replay with idempotent keys; surface failures per item.

14.5 AI UI — intent → proposal → review → undo

AI consumes your contract. Ambiguous APIs become industrial defects. Agent UX pattern:

  1. Intent — user asks or triggers a tool
  2. Proposal — streamed output with cancel
  3. Review — diff / citations / preview primary
  4. Apply — explicit
  5. Undo — required
Rule Detail
Stream + cancel Don’t block the UI without an escape
Citations / provenance Show sources when claims matter
Tool side-effects Need approval (email send, delete, purchase)
Diff readable without color Textual +/- or labels; keyboard apply/reject
Trust metric Track reject/override rate—not accept rate alone
Disclosure Label AI-generated content when it matters for trust/safety

Case D — AI bulk edit: Diff primary; stream+cancel; Apply; Undo. Reject autocomplete that silently mutates. Steal Copilot/Cursor apply-review—not ghostwriter theater.

Failure modes: silent AI mutation; optimizing only “accept rate”; red/green-only hunks; unattended agent emails.

14.6 Mobile + AI + offline intersections

  • On flaky networks: stream with reconnect honesty; don’t fake completeness.
  • On mobile: large apply/reject targets; diff in a sheet; don’t require hover for review.
  • Permissions for mic/camera for multimodal AI: JIT + degraded text path.
  • Offline: queue AI requests only if you can fulfill later; otherwise disable with explanation.

14.7 Platform parity snapshot (interaction-relevant)

Concern Web iOS Android Must match?
Semantic color roles ✓ ✓ ✓ Yes
Toast soft-undo duration 5–10s 5–10s 5–10s Yes
Nav chrome Side/top Tab bar Nav bar No — native
Swipe-back Rare System System No — native
Focus ring geometry Focus visible Focus engine Focus engine Intent yes

14.8 Chapter 14 summary

  • Dual models: shared semantics, native gestures/chrome.
  • Gestures never exclusive; JIT permissions with degraded paths.
  • Offline is a designed state with sync and conflict prefer-when.
  • AI is propose → review → apply → undo; side-effects need approval; measure overrides.

Part III Review Questions

Part III Review Questions

A. Feedback, latency, undo & state (Ch. 10)

  1. Write the five phases of the feedback loop and name one failure mode for each.
  2. Give the ≤100ms rule and assign UI patterns to the five latency tiers (instant through long).
  3. When do you choose optimistic vs pessimistic UI? Give one product example of each and the failure if reversed.
  4. Define the three undo classes (soft, quarantine, hard) with durations/mechanisms and a prefer-when for each.
  5. List the seven baseline L6 states. For each, what must the UI show beyond a generic spinner or “No data”?
  6. Taxonomy drill: Distinguish never-used empty, true empty, filtered-to-zero, search zero, error, and denied. Write one headline + one CTA for each for a “Projects” list.
  7. A team uses one empty illustration for both “no projects yet” and “no projects match your filters.” What breaks, and how do you fix it?
  8. Why should toasts rarely steal focus? When is assertive interruption justified?

B. Search, filter, sort & pagination (Ch. 11)

  1. Why is Cmd-K not sufficient as a product search strategy? List at least five requirements of a complete search experience.
  2. Design URL parameters for a shareable filtered table view (query, filters, sort, page/cursor). When would you avoid putting filters in the URL?
  3. Compare pagination, load-more, and infinite scroll with prefer-when / avoid-when. Which is default for an accessible data table, and why?
  4. Write the zero-state matrix for: empty query, query with 0 hits, filters with 0 hits, query+filters with 0 hits, error, denied.
  5. What does “ranking honesty” require when the system applies fuzzy matching?

C. Selection, tables & DnD (Ch. 12)

  1. Explain scoped select-all vs select-everything. Write microcopy for both scopes on a filtered list of 1,842 items with 25 on the page.
  2. Specify keyboard behavior for multi-select with shift-range in a list.
  3. List semantic and interaction requirements for a production data table (headers, sticky, resize, inline edit, loading, filtered-to-zero).
  4. What must every drag-and-drop feature ship alongside the pointer gesture? Give two concrete peer patterns.
  5. Why do desktop reorderable lists prefer handles over whole-row drag?

D. Navigation, history, teaching, share, autosave, clipboard, notifications, collab (Ch. 13)

  1. Map progressive disclosure layers (primary → overflow → palette → settings) and give an example action for each in a project management app.
  2. Outline the four-step first-artifact teaching curriculum. Why reject onboarding carousels?
  3. Autosave vs explicit Save vs Draft/Publish—when is each appropriate? What save states must be visible?
  4. Tier notifications into critical interrupt, batched digest, and muteable. Assign: password reset, new comment, weekly tips, payment failed.
  5. For a sync conflict between two peers editing the same note, which conflict strategy (keep both / choose / merge) do you pick and why?
  6. What ACL information must a share sheet make impossible to miss before “Anyone with the link” is enabled?

E. Mobile, gestures, permissions, offline, AI (Ch. 14)

  1. What is meant by “dual device models, not shrunk desktop”? Name three things that should match across platforms and three that should not.
  2. State the swipe-action rule and the “vertical scroll wins” rule. How do they interact?
  3. Walk through a JIT permission flow including denial with a feature-degraded path (pick camera or notifications).
  4. What offline banner copy and conflict UI does Case H recommend? What is rejected?
  5. Diagram the AI interaction loop: intent → proposal → review → undo. Where do stream+cancel, citations, and tool approval attach?
  6. Why is reject/override rate a better trust metric than accept rate alone for AI apply UX?

F. Integration & critique

  1. Using the Part III laws (L5–L8, L9–L11, L14), critique this flow: User swipes to delete a shared document; no undo toast; confirm dialog says “Are you sure?”; on failure a toast appears and the row is empty/error-ambiguous.
  2. A mobile screen ports a desktop table with hover-only row actions, infinite scroll, and Cmd-Click multi-select only. List five concrete fixes.
  3. Apply craft ∝ trust × frequency: where would you spend the first engineering week—global Cmd-K ranking polish, checkout error recovery, or settings page animation? Justify.
  4. Fill a mini competitive craft scorecard (1–5) for your product vs one rival on: undo honesty, density honesty, core-action scent, and AI review honesty.
  5. Walk the decision cheat-sheet questions “Reversible?” and “AI side effect?” for: (a) archive issue, (b) charge card, (c) agent sends email to customer list.

G. Short design prompts (apply the playbooks)

  1. Spec the empty/zero/error taxonomy for a search results page in an e-commerce inventory admin (including denied and offline).
  2. Design selection + bulk bar + partial failure UI for “Archive 40 issues.”
  3. Write an APG-minded keyboard map for a grid with sortable headers and inline-edit cells.
  4. Specify notification center empty states: never used notifications vs zero unread vs muted-all.
  5. Propose conflict UI wireframe text for offline merge of a structured profile (name, title, bio)—field-level choose vs whole-document choose.

Part III Quick Reference

Topic Bias / number
Acknowledge ≤100ms
Soft undo toast 5–10s
Quarantine ~30d Trash (or product equivalent)
Motion fast / default / slow 100–150 / 150–250 / 300–400ms
Touch target ≥44×44 primary
Feedback loop trigger → ack → work → resolve → undo
Undo classes soft · quarantine · hard
Empty taxonomy never-used · true empty · filtered-to-zero · search zero · error · denied
Findability query · scope · filters · sort · pager + URL
Select-all scoped; show N; warn on match-all
DnD gesture ≤1 swipe; visible + keyboard peer

Critique checklist excerpt (interaction): State matrix complete? Feedback ≤100ms and right tier? Undo class matches blast? Scent of core action? Focus restore? Filtered-to-zero distinct from empty? AI side effects approved?

Part IV — Design Systems

Design systems turn taste into contracts. A page can be beautiful once; a product must stay coherent across squads, platforms, locales, and AI generators that will invent whatever your API leaves ambiguous. This part covers how tokens and component APIs are governed, what belongs in the core kit, and how internationalization is treated as a first-class systems concern—not a late RTL flip.

Companion examples: See the Part IV examples companion.

Chapter 15 — Tokens, APIs, Promotion, Governance

15.1 What a design system is for

A modern design system is opinionated infrastructure for outcomes. It is not a Figma sticker sheet, not a dump of one-off wrappers, and not a brand mood board. Its job is to:

  1. Encode semantic contracts (roles, density, elevation, tone) so product UI stays coherent.
  2. Make the right path the easy path for humans and codegen/AI.
  3. Scale decisions without requiring every squad to renegotiate focus, contrast, or destructive patterns.
  4. Version those decisions so change is a migration, not a Friday find-replace.

Law L12 applies: abstract after three real uses. Law L13 applies: version the contract. Premature abstraction creates prop soup; unversioned renames create industrial defects.

15.2 Token layers

Use three layers. Product code imports semantic tokens only.

Layer Contains Who consumes Example
Primitive Raw ramps, type steps, space scale Token pipeline only --blue-500, --space-16, --font-size-16
Semantic Roles mapped to primitives Product UI, components --color-text-primary, --space-field-gap
Component (rare) Component-scoped aliases Component internals --button-bg, --toast-duration-soft

Rules:

  • Roles, not hexes (L1). No raw palette in app CSS or component style props.
  • Code is source of truth for what ships. Figma Variables mirror token names; weekly drift check on renames.
  • Pipeline: Style Dictionary (or equivalent) → CSS custom properties + iOS/Android artifacts.
  • Theme layers (compose, don’t fork trees): brand → mode (light/dark) → high-contrast / forced-colors → rare campaign overlays. Marketing may fork expression; product Locked surfaces stay on semantic roles.

Density as token maps

Density is not “tighter padding somewhere.” It is a named map of space, control height, and type meta roles.

Density Control height Field gap Row padding Prefer when
comfortable 44–48px 16–24 Airy First-run, marketing-adjacent, empty states
compact 36–40px 12–16 Default product Daily tools, forms, settings
dense 28–32px 8–12 Tables/lists Power users, data grids (still meet touch targets on primary mobile CTAs)

Expose density as a semantic theme attribute (data-density / --density-* aliases), not ad-hoc px. Switching density must not invent new type sizes outside the locked scale—only map which roles and spacings apply.

15.3 Surface partition: Locked / Guided / Open

Partition Meaning Override policy
Locked Auth, checkout, destructive, focus/a11y primitives, money/identity No product restyle of validation, focus, or semantics
Guided Common patterns with documented escape hatches Prefer system; document why if forking
Open Experiments, one-offs, brand moments Label Open explicitly; promote or delete

Prefer systemize when: ≥3 real uses on a Locked or Guided surface.
Prefer leave local when: one-off experiment with unclear reuse.
Failure modes: shadow libraries or premature API.

15.4 Promotion pipeline

Promotion is how local craft becomes infrastructure.

Stage Artifact Requirements
Recipe Local implementation + short note Works in one product context; a11y baseline
Pattern Docs + a11y notes + do/don’t ≥3 consumers; states designed; keyboard path
Component Semver package + tests + Storybook Stable API; tokens only; CI gates; catalog entry

Do not wrap a third-party once “for consistency.” Prefer Radix / React Aria (or platform equivalents) for behavior; skin with tokens. Build only when the contract is missing.

15.5 Component API discipline

Good APIs are boring and exhaustive.

Principle Practice
Semantic props tone, size, density — not blue / big / tightish
Composition asChild / slot patterns where polymorphism is needed
Unions Exhaustive TypeScript unions; no synonym variants (primary ≠ brand ≠ cta)
Lint no-raw-color · no-synonym-variant · no-unlabeled-icon-button · no-banned-import · require-focus-visible
Catalog JSON min schema: { id, name, props[], tokens[], a11yKeyboard, do, dont, status } for humans + codegen

Synonym APIs become industrial defects when AI scales them (spine: AI consumes your contract).

15.6 Semver SLA

Bump Tokens Components
MAJOR Rename/remove semantic role, or change its meaning Breaking prop/behavior change
MINOR Add role or alias Additive props/variants
PATCH Primitive ramp tweak behind same semantic (visual diff required) Bugfix / a11y fix without API change

Deprecation: 90-day window; alias bridge (--old → --new); codemod for renames; CI fails on deprecated imports after sunset. Figma Variables rename the same week as code SoT. Watch override rate on affected components after migrations (Case E).

15.7 Budgets & lint as governance

Example targets (tune to your product, keep the idea):

  • Core kit JS ≤ 150KB gz incremental on critical paths.
  • No raw hex/px in app CSS (space/type/color via tokens).
  • Shared motion only via transform / opacity.
  • Dual-theme contrast audited for semantic text and non-text UI.

Lint is not optional taste—it is how Locked contracts survive growth.

15.8 Storybook definition of done (DoD)

A component is not “done” when it renders in one happy path. Storybook DoD:

Gate Requirement
CSF Named stories for default, each variant, each density, each tone
States Empty / loading / partial / error / disabled / offline (as applicable)
A11y addon No serious axe violations on stories for Locked components
Interaction Play functions for keyboard open/close, focus restore on Dialog/Menu
Docs Purpose, props table, do/don’t, tokens used, a11y keyboard map
RTL / pseudo-loc At least one story with long strings / dir="rtl" where layout can break
Themes Light + dark (and HC if you ship it)

15.9 Visual regression (VR)

Treat Chromatic-class tools as fail-the-PR gates for Locked primitives—not optional screenshots in a wiki.

Rule Practice
Scope Locked + high-traffic Guided components
Threshold Pixel budget agreed; intentional changes require review approval
Triggers Token PATCH (primitive ramp), component layout CSS, density map edits
Flake control Disable non-deterministic motion in VR stories; fixed dates in Intl stories

VR without semantic tokens is noise. Tokens without VR make “PATCH” a lie.

15.10 Analytics hooks on Locked CTAs

Instrumentation belongs in the system, not copy-pasted track() calls.

  • Locked primary CTAs (Pay, Sign in, Create, Delete confirm) emit cue → action → reward events with stable component_id + surface.
  • Prefer system wrappers that accept analyticsId over ad-hoc product hooks.
  • Measure find-rate of core actions without docs; pair with override rate when product forks Locked chrome.

15.11 Feature-flag UI states

Flags are product states—design them.

Flag effect UI requirement
Hidden feature Remove from IA; no dead nav
Partial rollout Same Locked patterns; avoid “beta chrome” that breaks contrast
Kill switch mid-session Explain + recover; don’t blank the page
Experiment variant Still AA; no dark-pattern variants on Locked trust paths

Document flag × component interactions in Storybook where behavior diverges.

15.12 Error boundaries, 404, crash templates

Systemize failure chrome so squads don’t invent panic UI.

Template Contents Notes
Route 404 Plain language, link home + primary workspace, optional search Not cute dead-ends without recovery
Error boundary What failed, retry, report, session preserve when possible Focus to heading; don’t trap
Crash / hard fail Status code honesty, support path Log correlation id for support
Permission denied Explain + settings/request access + degraded path Not a blank screen (L6)

These templates are Guided→Locked candidates: shared tone, focus, and analytics.

15.13 CMS / rich-text (RTE) content system

Marketing and help content will escape your React tree. Treat CMS as a consumer of the contract:

  • Map CMS blocks to system components (Heading roles, Callout/Banner, Button styles)—not freeform HTML soup.
  • Enforce contrast and heading order in RTE allowlists.
  • Images: require alt policy (see Chapter 19); decorative vs informative.
  • Don’t let CMS invent new button variants or raw hex.

15.14 RACI sketch (systems ops)

Concern A R C
Locked primitives + tokens Design Systems Systems eng Product design
Guided patterns Product design Squad eng Systems
A11y CI + lint Eng Eng Systems / a11y
Override-rate remediation Systems Product Eng
Lived-experience on Locked Research Research PM / Systems

15.15 Prefer-when: adopt vs build

Prefer adopt (behavior lib + token skin) Prefer build
Focus traps, menus, tabs, dialogs with APG maps Domain-specific Locked flows (CheckoutField)
Combobox / listbox primitives Unique data viz encodings your brand owns
Toast queues, portals Parity already broken by platform chrome

Don’t wrap once for consistency. Do ban synonym forks.

Chapter 16 — Component & Layout Inventory

This chapter names the core kit. If a squad invents a parallel Accordion or a third Toast, that is a governance failure—not creativity.

For each component: purpose, primary API knobs, do/don’t. States follow Law L6 unless noted.

16.1 Actions & navigation chrome

Component Purpose Do Don’t
Button Trigger an action tone (primary/secondary/destructive/ghost), size, visible label or aria-label; pending disables + in-place status Icon-only without name; synonym cta/brand; confirm-everything
Link Navigate Real <a href>; distinct from Button; external indicated when needed div onClick navigation; button-styled links for non-nav actions without reason
Breadcrumb Hierarchy scent Landmark/nav label; current page not a link Truncate middle without accessible full path
Nav shells App IA chrome Sidebar / top / tab bar as platform-appropriate; labels on primary items until learnability proven Icon-only primary nav; marketing bento inside tool chrome

Nav shell prefer-when: sidebar for multi-section pro tools; top for simpler IA; native tab bars on iOS/Android (parity matrix: chrome need not match web).

16.2 Form controls

Component Purpose Do Don’t
Field Label + control + help + error Visible label; aria-describedby for help/error; preserve input on error Placeholder-as-label
Input Single-line text Correct type/autocomplete; PM-friendly auth fields Disable paste on passwords
Textarea Multi-line Resize policy; character limits announced when enforced Auto-grow without max that breaks layout at 400% zoom
Select Choose one from list Native when sufficient; APG listbox when custom Fake select without keyboard map
Checkbox Multi-select options Group legend; indeterminate only for “partial children” Clickable row without name
Radio Exclusive choice Fieldset/legend; equal visual weight Card-radio without radio semantics
Switch Immediate binary setting Label states (on/off); don’t use for “submit form” Switch for navigation

Form layout matrix:

Layout Prefer when Avoid when
1-column Critical tasks, checkout, mobile, cognitive load Dense admin with many short fields and large viewports (still stack under reflow)
2-column Related short fields (city/postal), large screens Label/control misalignment; password + unrelated promo column

Gaps between: label→control 4–8; fields 16–24; groups 32+ (space tokens).

16.3 Disclosure & overlays

Component Purpose Do Don’t
Tabs Peer panels One tablist; arrow key APG; selected panel only in tab order Nested tabs; tabs for sequential wizards
Accordion Progressive disclosure Button headers; one or multi-expand policy documented Accordion as fake navigation
Dialog Modal task Focus trap; Escape; restore trigger; labelled title Stack modals; steal focus from typing for non-assertive noise
Sheet Mobile/contextual panel Same focus rules; drag handle ≠ only dismiss Sheet without visible close
Menu Actions on an object APG menu; typeahead when long Hover-only open on mobile
Popover Non-modal anchored content Focus return; dismissible Modal dialog dressed as popover
Tooltip Supplementary name/hint Keyboard accessible; never sole instruction Tooltips for errors or essential copy

Interruption rules: one modal at a time; toasts queue; never steal focus from typing unless assertive error.

16.4 Feedback & status

Component Purpose Do Don’t
Toast Transient acknowledgment / soft undo Queue; polite live region; 5–10s soft undo; actions keyboardable Move focus for every toast; toast-only hard failures
Banner Persistent inline status Role/status or alert as appropriate; dismiss + undo class match blast Color-only severity
Badge Count/meta marker Text alternative for counts; don’t animate seizure-risk Badge as only error signal
Chip Filter token / selected attribute Removable chips named; keyboard remove Chip clusters as primary IA
Avatar Person/entity Initials fallback; alt empty if adjacent name present Avatar-only identity without name in lists
Skeleton Loading placeholder Layout-matched to final content; respect reduced motion Shimmer as entertainment; mismatch causing layout jump

16.5 Data & wayfinding

Component Purpose Do Don’t
Table Tabular data Real <table> or APG grid; headers/scope; sticky headers careful with focus; keyboard cell nav when grid Div soup tables; color-only status columns
Pagination Move through sets Clear “Page X of Y” or equivalent; preserve filters in URL Infinite scroll only with no “footer” tasks / no keyboard equivalent

Pagination vs infinite vs load-more is an interaction decision (Part III); the components must support URL state and focus to results status.

16.6 Layout primitives

Prefer layout primitives over one-off flex soup.

Primitive Job Notes
Stack Vertical rhythm Gap from space tokens; align
Inline Horizontal cluster with wrap Gap; align baseline/center for controls
Cluster Wrapping group (chips, buttons) Prefer over manual wrap hacks
Grid 2D alignment Tokenized gaps; collapse columns via CQ/breakpoints
Cover / Frame (optional) Media aspect Don’t crop meaningful UI chrome

Product layouts should be content-shaped: quiet chrome, loud content. Cards are not default containers—use cards when they bound an interaction.

16.7 Container-query (CQ) recipes

Breakpoints on the viewport alone lie inside nested shells. Prefer container queries for component-local adaptation.

Recipe Behavior Prefer when
Toolbar responsive Icon-only → icon+label at min cqi Toolbars in resizable panes
Card meta demotion Drop side meta first; keep title + primary action Card lists in mixed widths
Form split 2-col → 1-col when container narrow Settings panels, not only viewport mobile
Data table Prioritize columns; overflow menu for secondary Wide tables in side-by-side layouts
Nav collapse Labels persist until proven; collapse to icons with accessible names Dense shells

Reflow laws still apply: usable at 320 CSS px and 400% zoom; DOM order = reading order; no essential 2D scroll (WCAG 1.4.10).

16.8 Platform parity matrix

Semantics match; chrome may differ.

Concern Web iOS Android Must match?
Semantic color roles ✓ ✓ ✓ Yes
Type roles (not px twin) ✓ ✓ ✓ Intent yes
Focus ring geometry Focus visible Focus engine Focus engine Intent yes
Density maps ✓ ✓ ✓ Yes (values may differ)
Toast soft-undo duration 5–10s 5–10s 5–10s Yes
Destructive confirm patterns Locked Locked Locked Yes
Nav chrome Side/top Tab bar Nav bar No — native
Swipe-back Rare System System No — native
Materials / blur Web tokens System materials System Intent; don’t fake poorly
RTE/CMS blocks Web Limited Limited Shared content rules

Company bet: shared semantics; native gestures and nav. Reject pixel-identical RN fantasy as a default strategy.

16.9 Core kit status & contribution

Every named component above should exist once in the catalog with status: experimental | stable | deprecated. Contribution path = promotion pipeline (Chapter 15). Shadow libraries: promote or delete.

Chapter 17 — Internationalization

RTL flipping is necessary and insufficient. Locale-real products treat copy, grammar, formats, and layout expansion as systems problems.

17.1 Message architecture (ICU)

Use ICU MessageFormat (or equivalent) for all user-facing strings:

  • Plurals: one / other (and locale-specific categories: zero, few, many…). Never concatenate count + " items".
  • Select: gender/formality only when required by locale—and when you have real data, not stereotypes.
  • Variables: named placeholders; never rely on English word order.
  • Rich text: structured tags in messages (<link>) mapped to components—not HTML from translators.

API rule: components accept rendered strings or message IDs via a documented i18n layer—don’t embed English in Locked primitives.

17.2 Expansion budgets

Translated UI grows. Design for it.

UI element Budget guidance Failure if ignored
Buttons / tabs Allow ~30–40% growth; prefer wrap or taller control over ellipsis on critical actions Truncated “Save” equivalents; broken hit targets
Nav labels Prefer wrap/scroll patterns over icon-only fallback Unlearnable icons
Toasts / banners Multi-line allowed; max width tokenized Cut-off soft undo
Tables Column min-widths from content; horizontal scroll only as last resort with accessible strategy Unreadable cells
Dialogs Height grows with content; don’t lock to English screenshot Clipped primary actions

Pseudo-localization (below) is how you enforce budgets in CI/Storybook.

17.3 Locale formats with Intl

Never hand-roll dates, numbers, or currency.

Concern Use Notes
Dates/times Intl.DateTimeFormat Respect locale + user preference; absolute vs relative documented
Numbers Intl.NumberFormat Tabular figures in product tables (visual system)
Currency Intl.NumberFormat with style: 'currency' Currency code clarity when multi-currency
Lists Intl.ListFormat “A, B, and C” varies
Rel. time Intl.RelativeTimeFormat “3 days ago” — still provide absolute on demand for trust paths
Collation Intl.Collator Sort names correctly

Server and client must agree on timezone display rules for money/legal timestamps.

17.4 Pseudo-localization gates

Pseudo-loc is a ship gate, not a demo.

Technique Catches
Accents + wrapped brackets [!!! Hello !!!] Hardcoded strings, clipping
Padding (xxxHello Worldxxx) Expansion overflow
Bidirectional marks / fake RTL Mirroring bugs, mixed bidi
Long German-like compounds Layout breaks in nav/tables

Run pseudo-loc stories in Storybook DoD; fail PRs when Locked surfaces clip primary actions.

17.5 Logical CSS, RTL, and mixed bidi

  • Prefer logical properties (margin-inline-start, inset-inline-end, padding-block) over physical left/right.
  • dir="rtl" on document or islands; don’t mirror meaning-bearing icons incorrectly (e.g. media play vs back chevrons—follow platform conventions).
  • Mixed bidi: usernames, URLs, code, and phone numbers inside RTL prose need isolation (dir="auto" / bidi isolates) so punctuation doesn’t jump.
  • Truncation: ellipsis logically (text-overflow) with accessible full text on focus/hover and a non-hover path (title alone is insufficient for touch/AT).

17.6 Truncation strategy

Content Strategy
Critical action labels Prefer don’t truncate; wrap
Secondary meta Truncate with full text available to AT (aria-label or visually hidden)
Primary titles in lists Truncate end; ensure name is still unique enough in SR list
Numbers/currency Don’t truncate mid-value; abbreviate with clear format or wrap
Breadcrumbs Collapse middle with accessible full path

17.7 i18n × a11y × systems checklist

  • Lang attribute correct on page and on language islands.
  • Screenshots in docs are not the source of layout truth—pseudo-loc is.
  • VoiceOver/TalkBack smoke includes a non-English locale on critical paths quarterly when you ship those locales.
  • CMS content: translators use the same expansion rules; RTE doesn’t assume English line breaks.

17.8 Prefer-when

Prefer When
Full ICU + Intl from day one Any product that will leave one locale
English-only hardcode Throwaway internal spike labeled Open with delete date
Pixel-perfect English layouts Never for Locked surfaces

Part V — Accessibility & Inclusion

Accessibility is quality, not a compliance theater overlay. Exclusion is a defect. WCAG/EAA (and ADA/508 by market) are floors; lived experience is a gate on paths disabled people must complete.

Companion examples: See the Part V examples companion.

Chapter 18 — Inclusive Design Philosophy & Verification

18.1 Philosophy

  1. Situational disability is normal — bright sun, one-handed commute, noisy rooms, temporary injury. Designing only for “permanent disability personas” under-scopes reality.
  2. Nothing about us without us — paid participants with relevant disabilities on critical paths; findings can block ship on Locked surfaces.
  3. AA floor / humane ceiling — meet WCAG 2.2 AA baseline; exceed where trust × frequency demands (GOV.UK-style plain language, Error Summary, one-column critical tasks).
  4. Bake into primitives — contrast-gated tokens, focus rings, labeled APIs, APG keyboard maps. Squads should not reinvent accessible Dialog each quarter.
  5. Checklist floor vs lived-experience gate — automated/axe floor always; lived experience required when the path is essential (auth, pay, create, delete, appeal).

Failure mode: axe-green, unusable. Inclusion beats compliance theater.

18.2 Legal & market floors

Instrument Role
WCAG 2.2 AA Baseline success criteria
EAA / ADA / Section 508 Market-triggered legal obligations
VPAT / ACR Enterprise sales evidence
Internal ship gates Stronger than marketing claims

Legal compliance ≠ product quality, but ignoring legal floors is not a strategy.

18.3 AT matrix (verification environments)

Priority Combination Use
P0 VoiceOver + Safari Apple ecosystem
P0 NVDA + Chrome/Firefox Windows baseline
P0 TalkBack + Chrome Android
P1 JAWS + Chrome/FF Enterprise sales
P1 Voice Control (once per release train) Mobile core path
P2 Switch access / keyboard-only marathon Motor; Locked flows

Run SR smoke on auth / checkout / create each release:

  1. Land on page → skip to main
  2. Complete primary CTA
  3. Hear errors
  4. Dismiss modal → focus restored

18.4 Ship gates (release-blocking on critical paths)

Gate Bar
Keyboard task pass Complete job without pointer
Axe (or equiv.) Clean of serious issues on path
Dual-theme contrast Text 4.5:1 / large 3:1; UI non-text 3:1
Focus visible ≥2px contrast-aware ring; no outline: none without replacement
SR smoke Script above passes
Forced-colors / HC Product UI doesn’t force broken hex; system semantics preserved

18.5 Dual verification model

Layer Answers Cannot answer alone
Automated + checklist Contrast, name/role/value gaps, many ARIA mistakes Real task success, cognitive load, AT quirk survivability
Lived experience Can a person complete the job with their tools? Exhaustive bug coverage of every page

Cadence: paid sessions on critical paths each quarter; P0 findings block Locked ship.

18.6 Ownership

Eng owns a11y CI + lint (R); Design Systems owns accessible primitives (A); Research owns lived-experience sessions (R); PM owns that metrics don’t incentivize exclusion (A).

Chapter 19 — Structure, Focus, Name/Role/Value

Structure is accessibility. If the outline is fiction, every later fix is expensive.

19.1 Landmarks & skip links

Landmark Role / element Rules
Banner header / role="banner" Once per page for site header
Navigation nav Label multiple navs (aria-label)
Main main Exactly one; skip link target #main
Complementary aside Label if multiple
Contentinfo footer Site footer
Search role="search" When a search region exists
Form form Name when multiple forms

Skip completeness: skip to main required; consider skip to search or primary nav on dense tools. Skip links must be keyboard-visible on focus.

19.2 Heading hierarchy

Law Detail
One h1 Page purpose
No level skips for convenience Don’t jump h2 → h4 because of style
Style ≠ level Visual title uses type roles; heading level follows outline
Sections Prefer sectioning with headings over aria-label alone for long content

CMS/RTE must enforce heading allowlists (Chapter 15).

19.3 Focus management

Focus is a cursor (L9). Sticky headers and cookie banners must not fully obscure the focused control (WCAG 2.4.11)—see §20.13.

Rule Practice
DOM order = reading/tab order Don’t invent visual order that lies
Focus visible Contrast-aware ring ≥2px
Modals Trap; Escape; restore trigger (APG dialog)
Route changes Move focus to h1 or main; announce new page title via document.title + focus; optional polite status “Navigated to {title}” for SR users
Delete/destroy Announce result; restore sensibly—not document.body
Interruptions Don’t steal focus from typing unless assertive error

Native first, APG second (L10): use native elements; if you fake roles, you own the full keyboard map.

19.4 CSS order and flex/grid traps

order, positive tabindex, and absolute positioning create keyboard/AT order ≠ visual order bugs (WCAG 1.3.2 / 2.4.3 class failures).

Prefer Avoid
Reorder in DOM for responsive stacking order to shuffle tab sequence
Visual CSS that preserves sequence Positive tabindex except 0/-1 carefully
Sticky columns that don’t break reading Focusable elements inside aria-hidden

Add a lint/review checklist item: any order: in product CSS needs justification.

19.5 Name, role, value

Every interactive control needs an accessible name, correct role, and updated value/state.

Control Name from State
Icon button aria-label or visible text aria-pressed / expanded as needed
Input <label for> aria-invalid, describedby errors
Custom checkbox APG pattern aria-checked
Tabs Tab name aria-selected

Anti-pattern: ARIA div theater—divs with roles but incomplete keyboard support.

19.6 Product alt / accessible name matrix

Content Alt / name policy
Decorative image / empty-state art alt="" (and not focusable)
Informative image Concise alt of purpose, not “image of”
Complex diagram Short alt + long description link/table
Icon next to visible text Empty alt / aria-hidden on icon
Icon-only control Non-empty accessible name
Avatar beside name Empty alt
Avatar alone Name of person/entity
Chart See Chapter 20 summary + table fallback
CAPTCHA image Don’t — provide non-visual alternative

19.7 Forms structure

  • Visible labels (not placeholder-only).
  • Group related controls with fieldset/legend.
  • Error Summary pattern (GOV.UK): list errors linked to fields; focus management to summary or first error.
  • Preserve input on failure; field-local errors + retry.

Chapter 20 — Perception, Motor, Cognitive, Media

20.1 Perception: contrast, reflow, multi-channel

Requirement Spec / practice
Text contrast 4.5:1 normal · 3:1 large (1.4.3)
Non-text UI 3:1 (1.4.11)
Dark theme Separate tonal ramps—not inverted light; dual-theme audit
Forced-colors Don’t force hex; preserve ButtonText / Canvas semantics
Reflow 320 CSS px / 400% zoom; stack; no essential 2D scroll (1.4.10)
Color not alone (L11) Text, icon, and/or pattern with color

Glass/blur: overlays only; solid for data.

20.2 Live regions matrix (WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages)

Type Role / aria-live Use Avoid
Status status / polite Toasts, “Saved”, soft undo Flooding every keystroke
Alert alert / assertive Blocking errors, session expiry warnings Routine confirmations
Log log Sequential feeds (chat) Using log for one-shot errors
Progressbar native / APG Determinate long tasks Spinning with no name

Discipline: polite by default; assertive sparingly. Toasts should not move focus unless assertive error requires it.

20.3 Charts & data viz a11y

Layer Requirement
Encoding Position/length first; color + labels; patterns/textures for categories
Summary Text summary of the takeaway
Fallback Data table alternative (visually or linked)
Interaction Keyboard to data points if interactive; not hover-only
Themes Dual-theme contrast for series

Color-only charts are an anti-pattern.

20.4 Motor: pointer, touch, voice, switch, DnD

Concern Practice
Touch targets ≥44×44 primary controls
Pointer cancellation (2.5.2) No irreversible on pointerdown alone; allow cancel/undo
Spacing Avoid adjacent tiny targets; density maps still respect primary targets on touch
Hold-only Provide alternative to long-press-only actions
Gestures ≤1 swipe action per list row; visible button equivalent; vertical scroll wins
Desktop reorder Handles, not drag-only discovery
Voice Control Visible names match spoken labels; avoid unlabeled icons
Switch access Operable via keyboard path; no timing-only traps

Accessible drag-and-drop

Requirement Detail
Keyboard alternative Move up/down or “Move to…” menu
Drop feedback Multi-channel (text + visual); live region for result
Handles Discoverable grip with name
Cancel Escape restores
Screen reader Announce grab, target, drop

20.5 Cognitive patterns

Pattern Practice
One primary action Per view for critical tasks
Predictable chrome Same nav/help locations (3.2.3/3.2.4 class intent)
Chunking Wizards with progress; don’t dump expert surfaces
Plain language Especially errors and legal
Error Summary Linked list of errors
Quiet mode Reduce non-essential motion/badges/notifications when offered
Session restore Don’t punish timeouts with total data loss (see below)
Opinionated defaults Infinite settings is an anti-pattern; teach progressive disclosure

20.6 Timeouts & sessions

Step Requirement
Warn Before expiry, clear warning (alert) with time remaining
Extend Primary action to continue session
Preserve Restore drafts/inputs where possible after re-auth
Avoid Silent logout mid-form; timing that cannot be extended (unless essential security with alternatives)

Map to WCAG 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable intent on product sessions.

20.7 Motion & seizure safety

  • Motion tokens: fast 100–150 · default 150–250 · slow 300–400 ms.
  • Honor prefers-reduced-motion: opacity/instant alternatives.
  • No content flashing >3 times/sec.
  • Marketing scroll storytelling must not trap keyboard users or require motion to understand content.

20.8 Media players

Must have Notes
Captions Accuracy bar: speech + speaker ID when multi-speaker
Transcript For audio/video information
Keyboard operable controls Play/pause/seek/mute/volume/captions
No autoplay with sound Respect user/system settings
Description When visuals convey unique info

20.9 PDF & export a11y

Export type Requirement
PDF Tagged PDF when promised; reading order; headings; alt text; don’t ship scan-only as accessible
CSV/XLSX Prefer for data tables; document encoding
Image export Not an accessibility strategy for data

If the product claims “download accessible report,” verify with AT—not screenshots.

20.10 Auth & CAPTCHA (Case F)

Prefer Avoid
Passkeys / email OTP Puzzle CAPTCHA only
Visible labels + password-manager autocomplete Disable paste; placeholder-only
Always an accessible alternative if challenge required “Blind users are edge cases”
Measure completion by AT users and overall conversion Conversion-only A/B that hides exclusion

20.11 Help mechanisms (WCAG 3.2.6)

Help must be consistent in placement and identification across pages when provided.

Mechanism Notes
Human contact Same location/label across pages
Self-help / FAQ Reachable from a consistent control
Chatbot Disclose AI; provide human escalation; don’t block AT
Inline field help Associated via aria-describedby; not hover-only

Critical paths: denial and error states include a help/settings link—not dead ends (permissions JIT pattern).

20.12 Part V synthesis: bake, verify, include

  1. Bake into tokens and Locked components.
  2. Verify with gates + AT matrix.
  3. Include lived experience as a ship gate where it matters.
  4. Structure (landmarks/headings/focus/name) before ornament.
  5. Perception, motor, cognitive, and media are peer concerns—not backlog leftovers.

20.13 WCAG 2.2 additions (teach explicitly)

SC Level Practice in this book
2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum) AA Sticky headers/cookie banners must not fully obscure focused items; scroll focused into view
2.5.7 Dragging Movements AA Every drag path has a single-pointer non-drag alternative (Ch 12 DnD peers)
2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) AA 24×24 floor; product craft still aims 44×44 on primary
3.3.7 Accessible Authentication AA No cognitive function test (puzzles) as only auth; passkeys/OTP/PM-friendly (Case F)
3.3.8 Accessible Authentication (Enhanced) AAA Stricter; label AAA if claimed
3.2.6 Help Mechanisms AAA Consistent help placement; craft on Locked even when claiming AA only

Review questions (Parts IV–V)

  1. Tokens & governance: A squad wants to rename --color-accent to --color-brand and change it from “primary action” to “marketing highlight.” What semver bump is this, what deprecation steps are required, and why is Figma Variables timing part of the SLA?

  2. Promotion & inventory: You find three local implementations of a filter chip. Using the recipe → pattern → component pipeline and the core kit rules, what must exist before a Locked Chip ships (Storybook DoD, API knobs, do/don’t)?

  3. Layout & parity: Design a settings form that is 2-column on wide containers but must reflow at 320px / 400% zoom. Which layout primitives and container-query recipes apply, and which parity matrix rows must stay consistent on iOS/Android even if nav chrome differs?

  4. Internationalization: English UI says “1 seat” / “12 seats” beside a price. Specify the ICU plural approach, an expansion budget for the price button, which Intl APIs format the money and date of renewal, and how pseudo-loc would catch a hardcoded string in CI.

  5. Accessibility verification: A checkout PR is axe-clean but a VoiceOver user cannot complete Pay. Which philosophy tension applies, which ship gates failed, and what structure/focus/live-region/CAPTCHA checks would you run from Chapters 18–20 before allowing merge?

End of Parts IV–V.

Part VI — Practice

Chapters 21–25
Source: /workspace/research/modern-ui-research.md (Round 3 + completeness gap audit)
Spine reminder: Modern UI is opinionated infrastructure for outcomes—Clear, Talkative, Reversible, Systematic, Inclusive, Measurable.

Use this part with the Decision cheat-sheet and PR critique checklist (Ch 24) open. Every case lists choice, rejected alternative, lenses, steal mechanic, and measure—skipping rejects collapses pedagogy into taste.

Companion examples: See the Part VI examples companion.

Chapter 21 — Worked Decisions (Cases A–K)

Each case is a shipping decision under constraint. Read the rejected column as seriously as the choice: that is where trust, a11y, and systems debt hide.

Case A — Checkout (trust × frequency)

Context: Payment / identity-adjacent path. Craft ∝ trust × frequency (L14). Pessimistic default. Locked surface.

Lens Choice Rejected
Visual Quiet chrome; tabular figures for money; single Pay accent; solid surfaces for fields (no glass on data) Marketing gradient behind card fields; decorative bento competing with amounts
Interaction Pessimistic submit; idempotent pay keys; field-local errors + Error Summary; disable + in-place pending; receipt as resolve Optimistic “Paid!” before bank settles; toast-only failure; double-submit allowed
Systems Locked CheckoutField / PayButton; semantic tokens only; no product restyle of validation Squad-level validation restyle; synonym variant="primary"|"brand"|"cta"
A11y Visible labels; keyboard complete; aria-describedby for errors; 4.5:1 both themes; SR smoke on pay path Placeholder-only labels; color-only invalid; focus lost after error
Strategy Polish early in trust markets; ban growth tricks on Pay; PM owns payment success + chargebacks A/B fake scarcity on Pay; decoy urgency countdown

Steal mechanic: Stripe Checkout—field honesty, label+error pairing, docs-as-product clarity—not the marketing site’s gradients inside the form.

Measure: payment success · error recovery rate · keyboard completion · chargebacks / support “I was charged twice.”

Prefer-when reminder: Optimistic UI is wrong here even if it “feels fast.” Cheap rollback does not exist once money moves.

Case B — Empty → first artifact → habit

Context: First-run and return cue. Curriculum: identity → artifact → share → return. Air before density.

Lens Choice Rejected
Visual Air + one primary CTA; templates as simulated future; decorative empty art with alt="" 12-step carousel; permanent empty illustration with no action; card-grid of twelve starters
Interaction One undoable first create; return lands on artifact or clear next step Hard commit with no revert; onboarding that ends on a dashboard of zeros
Systems Empty-state recipe in system docs (never-used vs filtered-zero vs error vs denied) One-off snowflake empty per squad
A11y Named CTA in accessible name; skip link still reaches main; focus on primary create ASCII-only empty; icon button “+” without name
Strategy Optimize time-to-first-artifact and D7 return; starve confetti theater Activation vanity (modal tours) that never produce an object

Steal mechanic: Notion / Figma templates—start from a real artifact shape, not a slideshow.

Measure: time-to-first-artifact · D7 return · find-rate of create without docs · tour completion (vanity—do not optimize alone).

State distinction: True empty (never used) ≠ zero with filters (Case I) ≠ error ≠ denied. Each needs a different CTA.

Case C — Shared destructive delete

Context: Team-visible destroy or high blast radius. Trust > convenience. Confirm or quarantine—never soft toast alone.

Lens Choice Rejected
Visual Danger zone patterning; plain-language blast radius (“Deletes for 12 members”); no playful illustration Cute trash animation that minimizes consequence
Interaction Confirm with blast radius or Trash quarantine 30d if recoverable; announce result; restore focus to trigger Soft 5s toast for team-visible destroy; one-click delete for “speed”
Systems Locked DestructiveConfirm dialog (APG); shared copy patterns Per-page custom scary modals; Open overrides on Locked
A11y Focus trap; role="dialog" + labelled title; result in live region; focus restore—not body outline: none; focus dumped on document
Strategy Support undo log / audit for shared resources; trust NPS on delete flows Ship delete speed as a growth win

Steal mechanic: GitHub dangerous zone (typed confirm when irreversible); Google Drive Trash (quarantine when recoverable). Pick the class that matches recoverability—do not mix.

Measure: accidental-delete tickets · undo/quarantine restore rate · keyboard completion of confirm · time-to-recover.

Undo class map: Soft toast (5–10s) for local reversible · Quarantine 30d for recoverable shared · Hard confirm for external irreversibility (prod destroy, mass mail, legal erase—see Case J).

Case D — AI bulk edit proposal

Context: Agent or model proposes multi-file or multi-record mutation. Loop: intent → proposal → review → undo. Ambiguous APIs become industrial defects.

Lens Choice Rejected
Visual Diff as primary surface; readable without color (icons/text + patterns); density honest Ghostwriter theater; red/green-only hunks
Interaction Stream + cancel; Apply explicit; Undo after apply; tool side-effects need approval Autocomplete silently mutates; agent emails customers unattended
Systems Proposal object in contract (diff, scope, sideEffects[]); Guided pattern → promote after 3 uses One-off “AI magic” panel per feature
A11y Keyboard apply/reject; hunks announced; not color-only status Mouse-only accept-all
Strategy Track reject/override rate as trust metric; never optimize accept rate alone Leaderboard for “AI acceptance %”

Steal mechanic: Copilot / Cursor apply-review—human remains the authority on side effects—not autocomplete that writes production truth silently.

Measure: override/reject rate · undo after apply · side-effect incidents · time-to-review large diffs · trust NPS on AI features.

Case E — Token rename (systems ops)

Context: Semantic token or component API rename. Code is SoT. Semver + 90-day deprecation. AI consumers amplify bad renames.

Lens Choice Rejected
Visual / contract Meaning of role unchanged → PATCH behind same semantic; rename/remove/meaning change → MAJOR “Just tweak the hex” that changes role meaning without MAJOR
Interaction Codemod + alias bridge --old → --new; product UI keeps working during window Big-bang find-replace Friday; broken theme for a week
Systems Alias + 90-day deprecate; CI ban on deprecated imports after sunset; Figma Variables renamed same week as code Design library drifts 3 months; eternal dual APIs
A11y Contrast gates still pass both themes after ramp tweak; visual regression required on PATCH Unreviewed dark-theme breakage
Strategy Watch override-rate on affected components; Systems accountable (A), Product consulted (C) Ignore forks until shadow libraries bloom

Steal mechanic: Style Dictionary + semver discipline from mature kits (Polaris / Spectrum / Carbon contribution models)—promotion and deprecation as ops, not hero refactors.

Measure: deprecated-import CI failures · override rate · drift check (Figma vs code) · time-to-sunset · visual-regression fails caught pre-merge.

Token bump rules: MAJOR = rename/remove or change meaning of a semantic role · MINOR = add role/alias · PATCH = primitive ramp tweak behind same semantic (diff required).

Case F — CAPTCHA vs conversion (a11y × growth)

Context: Fraud pressure vs completion. Situational disability is real. “Blind users are edge” is a defect statement.

Lens Choice Rejected
Visual Auth chrome quiet; visible labels; PM-friendly fields Puzzle widget as hero of the page
Interaction Passkey / email OTP first; human review fallback; if challenge required, always accessible alternative Puzzle CAPTCHA only; hold-only / visual-only challenges
Systems Auth primitives Locked; CAPTCHA vendor behind adapter with alt path required in API Open paste of vendor iframe without alt contract
A11y Non-visual alternative always; measure completion by AT users; SR smoke on auth Conversion-only A/B that hides AT failure
Strategy Fraud metrics and AT completion; inclusion can block ship Ship puzzle-only because bounce rate looked fine in aggregate

Steal mechanic: Passkeys / OTP patterns with documented fallback—GOV.UK-style plain language if challenge explanation is needed—not “prove you’re human” theater.

Measure: overall conversion · AT-user completion · fraud catch rate · auth support tickets · time-to-OTP success.

Case G — Honest paywall (growth vs trust)

Context: Monetization surface adjacent to trust. Growth vs trust tension: clear value and reversible trials beat urgency theater.

Lens Choice Rejected
Visual Comparable plan columns; labeled default; AA contrast; no Locked checkout token overrides Purple glass paywall; decoy “Most popular” trap styling
Interaction Cancel path ≥ as clear as upgrade; trial terms reversible as promised; honest default Hidden cancel; autocharge obfuscation; fake countdown
Systems Guided marketing surface; checkout itself stays Locked Campaign theme breaking PayButton contract
A11y Keyboard compare + subscribe; price not color-only; focus order matches reading order Inaccessible pricing table; expand-only hover details
Strategy Experiments may lift trial→paid only if cancel clarity and billing trust metrics do not worsen Optimize activation while “how do I cancel?” tickets spike

Steal mechanic: Notion / Linear pricing clarity—labeled default, comparable outcomes, cancel discoverable—not dark-pattern playbooks.

Measure: trial→paid · cancel completion · support “how do I cancel?” · chargebacks · trust NPS on billing.

Competitive craft scorecard (example fill):

Dimension (1–5) Us Rival A Rival B
Trust-path quality 4 5 3
Density honesty 5 3 4
Opinionated defaults 4 4 2
Undo honesty 5 3 4
Checkout a11y 4 5 2
Core-action scent 5 4 3

Ship/kill UI bets from gaps—not from taste debates.

Case H — Sync conflict (offline)

Context: Offline queue then conflict. L6 state matrix must include syncing and offline. Prefer-when for resolution strategy.

Lens Choice Rejected
Visual Persistent banner “Offline—changes queued”; conflict UI shows both versions with clear labels Spinner with no meaning; silent badge
Interaction On conflict: keep both (equal peer edits, unknown merge) · choose (one clearly stale) · merge (structured fields, no overlapping prose); keyboard-accessible Silent overwrite; drag-only merge
Systems Sync indicator required in shell pattern; conflict pattern Guided → Locked if ≥3 products Ad-hoc per-entity conflict modals
A11y Banner as status (polite); conflict dialog per APG; choices named Color-only “out of sync” dot
Strategy Data integrity > faux realtime; measure conflict rate and resolve success Hide conflicts to protect “delight” metrics

Steal mechanic: Collaborative editors that surface presence + conflict explicitly (Figma-style conversation of state)—not last-write-wins pretending to be magic.

Measure: conflict rate · resolve success without data loss · time-to-ack offline · support “my edits vanished.”

Case I — Search zero-with-filters (findability)

Context: Information-seeking path. Cmd-K ≠ full search product. Query / scope / empty / zero-with-filters / ranking honesty are distinct. Completeness gap: filter recovery.

Lens Choice Rejected
Visual Results list flat and scannable; active filters as dismissible chips; zero-state explains filters, not “no content in product” Same empty illustration as never-used; card-grid of unrelated upsells
Interaction Distinguish: no query yet · zero for query · zero with filters on · error/timeout; primary CTA on filtered-zero = Clear filters (preserve query); URL persists q + facets; ranking honesty (no fake fullness) One generic “No results”; auto-clear filters silently; infinite skeleton
Systems Search/filter pattern in docs: chip/sheet filters, scoped select, URL schema; promote when ≥3 surfaces Each squad invents facet UX; Open overrides on Locked result row
A11y Combobox/listbox per APG (or native); live region announces result count; chips keyboard-dismissible; don’t rely on color for “active filter” Hover-only facet panel; count not announced; focus lost on refine
Strategy Measure find-rate without docs; refine abandonment; “clear filters” usage; starve search theater (pretty empty, weak retrieval) Optimize search engagement clicks that aren’t successful finds

Decision tree (ship this):

  1. If filters.active && results.length === 0 → copy: “No matches with current filters” + Clear filters + optional “Clear all” + show chip list.
  2. If !filters.active && query && results.length === 0 → copy: “No matches for ‘{q}’” + suggestions / spelling / broader scope.
  3. If !query && !filters → search empty coaching (examples), not product-empty art.
  4. If error → retry + status, never masquerade as zero.

Steal mechanic: Faceted search recovery from mature commerce/docs search—filter chips + clear as first-class—not Linear Cmd-K alone (command palette ≠ retrieval product).

Measure: find success · zero-with-filters recovery rate · clear-filter CTR · time-to-first-successful-open · queries-with-refine that end in open.

Case J — Account delete / data-rights

Context: Privacy and legal erase / export. ≠ soft-delete of a document (Case C). External irreversibility + compliance. Hard confirm class; quarantine may still apply for grace period if policy allows—but user-facing copy must match legal reality.

Lens Choice Rejected
Visual Settings → Privacy / Data rights IA; plain language consequences; no playful “bye” confetti that obscures permanence Buried link in paragraph footer; marketing illustration over legal copy
Interaction Preference center: export · download · delete account · consent minimize; delete = typed confirm or equivalent hard gate; show what is erased vs retained (billing/legal holds); email receipt of request; status timeline (requested → processing → done) Soft toast “Account deleted”; same flow as archive project; silent partial delete
Systems Locked DataRights patterns; audit log; do not reuse DestructiveConfirm copy from file delete without rights-specific strings Per-market snowflake; Open copy overrides on legal strings
A11y Keyboard complete; Error Summary if challenges fail; session timeout warn+extend on long export; SR announces request submitted Timer expires mid-export with no restore; puzzle gate with no alt (tie to Case F)
Strategy Trust & compliance > retention dark patterns; cancel/export/delete clarity co-owned by Legal + PM; VPAT/ACR if enterprise sells Trap cancel / hide delete to protect MAU; growth experiments on retention that block data-rights paths

Steal mechanic: Honest preference centers and account-delete flows that state retention exceptions plainly (export first, delete second)—GOV.UK plain language + Stripe-level receipt honesty—not “contact support to leave.”

Measure: time-to-complete export/delete · support tickets “how do I delete/export” · incomplete-request rate · complaints/regulatory · trust NPS on privacy settings.

Contrast with Case C: File/team delete → Soft / Quarantine / Hard by blast radius. Account erase → legal Hard (plus any policy grace window disclosed). Never ship account delete as a 5-second undo toast.
